newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ASEAN pushes Vietnam membership at APEC summit.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN pushes Vietnam membership at APEC summit.

text.p: Southeast Asian members of APEC pressed Asia-Pacific leaders at their summit on Monday to reconsider membership for Vietnam, Japanese sources said.

Philippine President Fidel Ramos, chairing the summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, said he would refer the case back to APEC ministers for review in Vancouver next year, said one Japanese source, who spoke to reporters on condition of anonymity.
"During lunch, a leader of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations brought up the subject of the membership schedule, and said he had Vietnam in mind," the Japanese source said.
Other leaders from ASEAN supported the move, the source said.
"The tone was that ASEAN could not wait three years before Vietnam, which is also an ASEAN member, entered APEC," said the Japanese source.

APEC ministers said on Saturday after a pre-summit meeting that the group would draft a set of conditions for new membership next year, announce successful candidates in 1998 and accept them as full members in 1999.

The call to reconsider the case of Vietnam fostered lively debate, with some leaders asking for similar consideration for Peru, the Japanese sources said. Others said the ministerial conference had dealt with the membership question and schedule.
The sources said there could be a change in the overall new membership schedule as the result of Monday's discussions.
ASEAN groups Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei and the Philippines. Vietnam is the only ASEAN member outside APEC.
The APEC leaders held their summit at Subic Bay, a former U.S. naval base north of Manila.
